name: Agarwal Toughened Glass India Limited
summary:
Rapid sales and accounting-profit expansion have not yet translated into cash. FY2026 revenue was ₹94.92 crore and PAT ₹21.60 crore, but operating cash flow was negative ₹8.50 crore. FY2022–26 cumulative CFO was negative ₹18.47 crore against ₹46.93 crore PAT. July equity and upfront warrant funding materially improve modeled survival; they do not prove collections or create a durable moat. At the official 19 October close ₹177.50, the linked base case yields approximately 6.38% annualised after assumed execution friction, below the 15% analytical hurdle. The bull case is attractive only with stronger utilisation, margins and cash conversion; the bear case loses approximately 63% of terminal share value despite remaining funded in the explicit scenario.

The appropriate research conclusion is a cash-conversion and disclosure watchlist, not a recommendation to implement. Historical reporting errors, inconsistent related-party totals and non-cooperation with rating agencies require follow-through. The later audited cash-flow comparative repairs the major FY2025 arithmetic problem; it would be wrong to say that specific error persists in FY2026 or to infer fraud.

Sources: [S1], [S5], [S6].

Observed official turnover permits a coarse liquidity band; large SME lot, circuits and concentrated participation prevent guaranteed execution.

Most reported receivables are under six months and some investment may support future capacity, but that does not establish collection or justify treating the pattern as transient.

sections.title: 1. Executive Verdict
sections.text:

FY2022–26 cumulative CFO was negative ₹18.47 crore against ₹46.93 crore PAT. sections.title: 2. Research Header, Gates and Data Confidence
sections.text:
NSE SME, symbol AGARWALTUF, ISIN INE0P8X01016. Accounts are standalone Indian GAAP, ₹crore unless stated. The proposed Dubai subsidiary was not treated as incorporated or as an operating contributor. Current issued shares are 19,326,466, verified by the exchange’s September listing approval; historical weighted-average EPS is not the current-share denominator. The input spreadsheet was undated and is not the quote source.

Integrity and reliability remain conditional, not blanket clean: rating information gaps, unreconciled related-party presentation and CSR wording are specific concerns. Funding is conditional on the dated capital bridge, existing bank-line continuation and the stated cash-availability assumptions. Tradability is conditional on SME lot/circuit and participant-concentration risks. There is no verified observed repayment default in the reviewed audit. Scenario default or financing stress must not be presented as an actual event. Primary historical inputs have medium confidence after scope reconciliation; forecasts have high economic uncertainty even when their inputs are traceable.

Sources: [S1], [S7], [S18].

sections.title: 3. Scorecard and Calculation Audit
sections.text:
BQS 5.08, GQS 5.00 after the persistent-cash-conversion cap (raw 6.40), and conditional IAS 3.97. Display rounded half-up to one decimal; use unrounded arithmetic for classification. Canonical factors: GOV 4, MOAT 5, REV 8, DUR 6, CAP 6, CASH 2, BAL 5, EXEC 5, EARN 6, R 2, D 5, P 3, L 7. All factors have Medium evidence confidence; forecast uncertainty remains High. No weights are renormalised. GOV4 does not trigger the governance cap. CASH2 reflects persistent, not isolated, cash absorption and caps GQS at5. IAS reuses BQS once; GQS is not an additional premium. A one-point move in GOV and CAP changes BQS by0.32 and IAS by0.08; a one-point change in R and D changes IAS by0.55. Interpret small score gaps as ties, not precision. Conditional ranking assumes the stated standalone scope, funded scenario mechanics and ₹5lakh reference position, not personal suitability.

Sources: [S1], [S3], [S18].

sections.title: 4. Business Overview
sections.text:
The Jaipur-based company processes purchased glass into toughened, laminated, insulated and other value-added products for construction and related applications. Economics depend on raw-glass procurement, utilisation/yield, processing quality, energy, delivery and customer collection. It is not economically identical to a primary float-glass manufacturer with captive upstream capacity. Material advances to suppliers and low trade-credit balances mean growth consumes shareholder or bank cash before customers pay.

IPO disclosures describe Unit I toughening capacity of 612,000 square metres and insulated-glass capacity of 90,000; Unit II toughening capacity of 1.08 million and laminated capacity of 150,000. Planned expansion capacity must not be added a second time to later management presentations. The FY2025 presentation described a ₹24 crore third manufacturing facility; the August 2026 update described Unit III warehousing equipment freeing space elsewhere. A reconciled commissioning/capacity bridge is still required. No solar-glass or Dubai revenue is inserted into the base case.

Sources: [S3], [S9], [S13].

sections.title: 5. Moat / Industry Position
sections.text:
The October 6 exchange filing includes an actual photograph of a Saint-Gobain Assured Processor certificate valid to 31 August 2027. This supports qualification and process capability, not exclusivity, guaranteed demand or pricing power. Contract wins and an operating plant provide a credible market position; alternative processors and cyclical construction demand limit the inference of a strong moat. Historical IPO top-ten customer concentration was 34.31% in FY2024 and 40.46% in H1 FY2025, not a verified current FY2026 concentration number.

Sejal Glass is a useful architectural-processing comparator, but its acquisitions and UAE operations differ. Its FY2026 consolidated core operating profit before interest/depreciation was ₹61.47 crore on ₹396.50 crore sales, about 15.5%, versus Agarwal’s approximately 29.6% excluding all other income. This difference deserves investigation, not automatic attribution to superior economics. Asahi India Glass FY2025 consolidated core EBITDA is approximately 16.7% on a much larger, integrated automotive/architectural base. Its ₹719.97 crore CFO demonstrates that a capital-intensive glass business can still convert profit into operating cash, while heavy capex can keep free cash negative. Neither peer’s market multiple is transferred without matched current quotes and accounting scope.

Sources: [S11], [S22], [S23].

sections.title: 6. Revenue Growth & Scale
sections.text:
Restated FY2022/23/24 revenues were ₹33.4094/39.9503/38.3278 crore; FY2025/26 audited revenues were ₹55.3062/94.9239 crore. The old issuer download named “Anual-report-21-22” actually contains signed FY2021 statements, with revenue ₹21.5820 crore versus FY2020 ₹27.8747 crore. Thus FY2021–26 CAGR is 34.48%, and FY2023–26 CAGR 33.44%. The pandemic trough makes the first endpoint flattering, but the separately disclosed three-year measure also exceeds 30%; it is not necessary to invent a second discretionary small-base penalty.

FY2026 sales growth was 71.6%. Management’s unaudited Q1 FY2027 sales update gives ₹34.40 crore against ₹28 crore a year earlier; an erroneous QoQ heading does not make this an audited sequential comparison. One quarter does not establish a sustained trajectory upgrade. Management’s June order book of ₹55 crore and 57% utilisation are attributed statements, not audited sales or cash. September’s ₹2.55 crore Relaxo order and October’s ₹4.24 crore medical-college order have March 2027 completion expectations; no disclosed collection schedule or margin validates treating them as cash already earned. Do not add them to an old order book without subtracting execution.

Sources: [S1], [S3], [S4], [S9], [S10], [S12].

sections.title: 7. Growth Quality & Reinvestment Runway
sections.text:
Construction, commercial glazing and higher-specification products provide accessible demand, but demand alone is not return on capital. Core EBITDA excluding other income grew from ₹3.60 crore FY2022 to ₹28.06 crore FY2026. Using 26% normalised tax, the FY2022–26 change in core NOPAT divided by the change in equity plus debt less cash is approximately 20.55%; retaining all cash in capital lowers this to 18.33%. This is an endpoint capital-efficiency indicator, not a mature project-cohort return. IPO cash, supplier advances, ramp-up dates and restrictions on deposits complicate the denominator. Against an analyst 15–18% capital-cost range, excess returns are plausible but not yet robustly demonstrated by realised free cash.

The model funds working capital explicitly. Opening broad operating WC is built from actual inventory, receivables and advances, excluding identified tax, interest, financial loans, incentive receivables and prepaids, less actual operating creditors. It is not manufactured by applying a forecast ratio backwards. Incremental positive sales absorb 70%/62%/85% in base/bull/bear. Falling sales do not generate an automatic cash release. This is deliberately less generous than converting the whole incentive receivable or supplier-advance balance into immediate cash.

Sources: [S1], [S3].

sections.title: 8. Management, Governance & Execution
sections.text:
Promoter-category votes at the 18 September AGM record date establish 11,670,600 shares out of 19,326,466, or 60.3866%. This is not relabelled as a September 30 shareholding pattern or pledge clearance. The increase from March’s 11,340,600 is consistent with preferential participation, not proof of market purchases. July equity/warrant terms dilute non-participants but provide actual financing; future conversion cash and corresponding shares must be paired.

CRISIL’s 28 April 2026 release revised ₹8.7 crore rated facilities to B/Stable, issuer not cooperating; CARE’s 29 January release retained B−, issuer not cooperating, for ₹6.55 crore. These are information-limited credit assessments, not proof of an observed default, and cannot be added as unused credit availability. The audit reports no repayment default or fraud identified in its work. Both sides of that evidence matter.

The corrected FY2025 annual summary changed related-party purchases from ₹5.0295 crore to ₹1.6295 crore, whereas detailed transactions and the later comparative retain ₹5.0295 crore. That ₹3.4 crore presentation discrepancy needs reconciliation. FY2026 related-party purchase/sale figures are stated including GST, so dividing them by net revenue would not give an exact exposure percentage. KMP remuneration of ₹64.8 lakh versus the employee-expense director line ₹69.6 lakh differs by ₹4.8 lakh; relative remuneration ₹32.4 lakh is separately disclosed. These discrepancies are not evidence of intentional misconduct on their own.

The secretarial report’s CSR remarks and the board’s response require a payment/compliance reconciliation alongside CARO’s language. No undisclosed penalty is invented. The September auditor appointment follows expiry of a one-year term and is not described as an adverse resignation. Two company-secretary changes are an execution/control observation, not an automatic integrity failure.

Sources: [S1], [S2], [S8], [S16], [S17].

sections.title: 9. Financial Forensics
sections.text:
Five-year PAT was ₹0.5018/0.9697/8.6852/15.1720/21.5975 crore; CFO was −₹0.9974/+2.2045/+6.9512/−18.1236/−8.5043 crore. Five-year cash capex was ₹26.7799 crore, leaving cumulative pre-financing free cash approximately negative ₹45.2495 crore. FY2026 receivables rose to ₹34.5435 crore, inventory ₹29.4060 crore and advances ₹36.6008 crore. Closing receivables equal about 133 days of annual sales; this is not an ageing measure. Note 11 separately reports ₹0.55 crore over six months, unchanged from FY2025, with most balances under six months. Missing confirmations are disclosed without a quantified affected amount.

The FY2025 corrected annual cash-flow statement showed CFO +₹14.7022 crore despite listed adjustments and a closing total inconsistent with its own components. The FY2026 audited comparative repairs it: 14.7022 + noncash adjustments 3.7345 − WC absorption 36.5603 = CFO −18.1236. Investing cash −12.7254 and financing +64.4020 yield net +33.5530; opening cash .3189 becomes 33.8719, matching the balance sheet. This is a material historical reporting problem now reconciled, not a reason to keep using the favourable old CFO.

FY2026 other income ₹5.1388 crore includes ₹4.1010 crore other operating income and ₹1.0028 crore deposit interest. A conservative core case removes all other income without claiming every rupee is nonrecurring. FY2025’s ₹1.333 crore deferred-tax credit boosted reported PAT. Normalised FY2026 PAT at 26% tax after excluding other income is approximately ₹18.16 crore. Incentive/reimbursement receivables ₹7.4369 crore are not assumed cash; the IPO’s older RIPS entitlement/receipt figures need a scheme-level bridge, not an allegation of excess claims.

Opening debt is ₹24.6744 crore, including current maturities once. Cash ₹10.6459 crore includes ₹9.0107 crore deposits. The model reserves ₹3.9845 crore unspent IPO machinery cash and uses it only for that project; a separate bound excludes the remaining deposits. Current “other provisions” ₹6.4823 crore are settled once; they are not claimed to be a precisely reconciled income-tax balance. Tax assets ₹0.5113 crore, incentives and prepaids receive no recovery credit. Other noncurrent liabilities ₹0.2284 crore are reserved against cash through exit, not assumed immediately due; reserve and claim offset at exit. Existing other current liabilities and audit accruals already sit in WC and are not paid again.

The May utilisation certificate identifies gross IPO ₹62.6356 crore, issue expenses ₹7 crore, object budget ₹55.6357 crore, cumulative use ₹51.6512 crore and balance ₹3.9845 crore. The annual table’s ₹4.5062 crore use is the second-half flow, not cumulative expenditure. The GST note says delayed-payment input-credit reversal was not made, with unestimated impact management considers immaterial; that is a specific unresolved tax question, not a quantified liability. IPO company VAT litigation of ₹0.189 crore is historical; later nil-contingency wording does not independently establish closure.

Sources: [S1], [S2], [S3], [S5].

sections.title: 10. Valuation & Market Expectations
sections.text:
At ₹177.50 and 1.9326466 crore issued shares, market capitalisation is ₹343.04 crore. Current-share P/E is 15.88 times reported FY2026 PAT and 18.89 times conservative core PAT. These earnings multiples do not establish cheapness when growth absorbs cash. A mechanical March-debt/cash EV cross-check is dated and must not silently add July funds as though they remained unspent in October.

July initial financing is ₹18.0053 crore equity plus ₹12.50775 crore warrant upfront payment, total ₹30.5130894 crore gross. The headline total issue size is not cash already received. Base/bull assume a further ₹37.52325 crore and 4.59 million shares in FY2028; the no-exercise case includes neither. The linked model deducts ₹1 crore assumed issue costs, taxes on future earnings, cash capex, WC, principal, old claims and stress losses. No unused rated facility is invented. Base margins decline from 26% to 25%, below FY2026 core margin; bear falls to 18–20%, bull 29–30%. Exit EV/core NOPAT multiples are 12/8/16 for base/bear/bull, not a borrowed peer P/E.

Base terminal price ₹238.27 gives 6.38% annualised over 4.44 years after 1% entry and exit friction, with no dividends; bull ₹544.12 gives 28.12%; bear ₹65.29 gives −20.53%. These are conditional scenarios, not price targets or personal return promises. The no-warrant base is funded and gives ₹275.45/9.91% because less cash is accompanied by less dilution. Three percentage points lower margins reduce the base to ₹203.61/2.68%; 15 additional percentage points of incremental WC absorption give ₹229.48/5.48%. Excluding all non-IPO deposits gives ₹236.17/6.16%.

Base entry prices meeting 12%/15%/18% hurdles are approximately ₹141/₹126/₹112, assumption-dependent, not observable fair values. The 15% hurdle requires about 30.74% uniform sales CAGR to FY2031, roughly ₹362.7 crore terminal revenue, with the same capex and margins; that calculation is not evidence the installed capacity can support it. The two-way margin/multiple grid and funding tests remain essential.

Sources: [S1], [S5], [S6], [S7], [S18].

sections.title: 11. Bear Case & Permanent-Loss Path
sections.text:
The severe case combines sales contraction, lower margins, sticky WC, 20% receivable and inventory cash losses, 25% supplier-advance loss and withdrawal of 25% of short-term bank funding, without a simultaneous WC cash release. It assumes no remaining warrant exercise. The specified case remains above the ₹3 crore cash buffer because July funding is included once and growth investment is curtailed. This is evidence for conditional survival, not immunity from bank withdrawal or undisclosed commitments. Terminal price is about 63.2% below entry. Permanent impairment can come from margins normalising, unrecoverable advances, expansion with no incremental return and further dilutive financing; a temporary quoted drawdown is not the same thing.

₹177.50 × 1,200-share lot is ₹213,000. All 60 official sessions have observations. The lower of mean and median turnover is the 60-day median ₹63.34 lakh; a ₹5 lakh exit at 5% participation is approximately 1.58 sessions, versus 3.95 at 2% and .79 at 10%. This is theoretical capacity, not executable depth. A ₹5 lakh reference position cannot be expressed exactly in whole lots. The eligible series has a 20% band; dormant-series rows do not create an active conflicting band. Named ASM/GSM/ESM lists do not contain the issuer on the checked dates, but the exchange’s participant-concentration and SME irregular-trading cautions remain relevant. The 19 October REG1 file applies to the next trading day, not retroactively to that day’s executions.

Sources: [S1], [S6], [S18], [S19], [S20], [S21].

sections.title: 12. 5× / 10× Feasibility
sections.text:
Fivefold and tenfold price gains over 4.44 years require approximately 43.7% and 68.0% annual compounding before friction. At full warrant conversion, target equity values would be about ₹2,123 crore and ₹4,245 crore. Holding the base terminal cash/debt bridge and 12 times NOPAT constant, these require roughly ₹170 crore and ₹347 crore NOPAT, implying approximately ₹935 crore and ₹1,891 crore sales at a 25% EBITDA margin and modeled depreciation. This is arithmetic, not accessible capacity. It substantially exceeds the base and bull operating plans; additional capital, dilution and implementation would have to be modeled rather than assumed away. A small starting market capitalisation alone does not make either outcome probable.

Sources: [S1], [S6].

sections.title: 13. Monitoring Plan
sections.text:
At the next half-year release, reconcile cash collections, supplier advances, inventory, incentive receivables and statutory/tax balances, not only PAT growth. Require a full current cash restriction and debt-maturity bridge after July proceeds. Track the remaining warrant exercise date, cash and corresponding shares together. Request a unit-by-unit capacity/commissioning/capex bridge for the third facility and any solar or Dubai project before attributing value. Reconcile the FY2025 related-party purchase difference, CSR payment evidence, tax-reversal exposure and historical VAT closure. A fresh rating supported by cooperation would improve funding evidence; merely renaming an old rating does not.

Downgrade the thesis if sales rise while CFO remains materially negative without verifiable recoverable investment, or if new commitments consume financing faster than modeled. Improve the cash factor only after actual sustained collections, not promises or a one-off financing receipt. Recompute liquidity for the intended position and current lot/circuit conditions before any implementation discussion.

Sources: [S1], [S9].

sections.title: 14. Final Classification & Conditional Action
sections.text:
Cash-conversion watchlist with conditional modeled returns below the analytical hurdle. Attractive revenue growth is real in the reviewed series, but funding it has required outside capital and reporting reconciliation. No trade instruction is made. A lower price alone can improve return arithmetic, not business quality; cleaner disclosures alone do not guarantee a good investment price. The next decision point is evidence of profitable cash conversion and disciplined deployment of the new capital, not another headline order announcement.

Sources: [S1], [S5], [S6].

sections.title: 15. Sources, Assumptions & Open Questions
sections.text:
Primary basis: FY2026 annual statements and audit notes; corrected FY2025 annual and later comparative; December 2024 final prospectus/restated statements; actual FY2021 signed accounts; May 2026 IPO-use certificate; July allotment and September exchange listing approval; AGM voting results; August operating update; September/October order and certificate filings; CRISIL and CARE releases; official dated NSE price/turnover/lot/surveillance files. Peer reports support economic context, not current relative valuation. All supplied spreadsheet metrics remain unverified historical intake, not primary evidence.

Material open items are current deposit restrictions and uses of July cash, precise supplier-advance composition, current lender commitments/maturities, remaining project obligations, full incentive entitlement/collection bridge, CSR/RPT reconciliations, current pledge disclosure and actual spread/depth. Model assumptions are identified as assumptions and exposed to downside tests. No probability-weighted scenario IRR is called an expected portfolio return; no personal tax or suitability conclusion is made.

Sources: [S1], [S2], [S3], [S4], [S5], [S6], [S7], [S8], [S9], [S10], [S11], [S12], [S13], [S14], [S15], [S16], [S17], [S18], [S19], [S20], [S21], [S22], [S23].

calculations.capital_return_caveat: Cash deduction is generous: earmarked or guarantee deposits are not necessarily surplus. Recompute with cash retained in capital as a lower-return bound; IPO cash and project ramp dates mean this is a multi-year endpoint indicator, not a mature cohort return.

assumptions.scope: Parent only. No Dubai, solar glass, or incremental third-line revenue explicitly added. Fiscal FY2027 revenue scenarios include the reported unaudited Q1 ₹34.40 crore, not annualized blindly. Starting balance sheet is March, not an invented October cash figure. July financing added once during FY27; actual subsequent cash use unknown, modeled through full-year expenses and investment.
assumptions.WC: Opening broad proxy uses actual inventory, receivables and advances less separately identified tax, interest, financial loans, subsidy and prepaid assets; deduct trade creditors, other current liabilities and audit fee payable. Supplier advances may contain capital items; keeping them in the opening WC floor does not create a cash release. Incremental sales consume 70/62/85% cash in base/bull/bear, no automatic release on falling sales. Subsidy and prepaids receive no refund or terminal credit.
assumptions.tax: Settle the full ₹6.4823 crore other current provisions once. Separately retain ₹0.2284 crore against unidentified noncurrent liabilities from opening cash through the terminal date; this is a cash reserve, not a claim that payment is immediately due. At exit, the reserved cash and corresponding liability offset and neither is credited again. This preserves the cash-available path without inventing an accelerated noncurrent maturity. Exclude ₹0.5113 crore tax assets from recovery. These are not called exact income-tax liabilities. New profits taxed at26%; no deferred-tax asset creation or tax refunds. Current provisions are not also deducted in opening WC apart from separately excluded audit fees.
assumptions.funding: March cash is upper bound before restrictions; ₹3.9845 crore IPO balance reserved to machinery. Gross July equity/upfront warrant receipt₹30.5130894 less analyst₹1 crore costs. Base/bull assume remaining₹37.52325 warrant cash and4.59m shares in FY28; no-exercise sensitivity is mandatory. Bear assumes no exercise. No new bank borrowing or unused rating facility assumed; existing working-capital lines roll, with stated principal and severe bear withdrawal.
assumptions.valuation: Core NOPAT enterprise multiple12/16/8; add cash only above₹3 crore buffer, subtract ordinary debt; no lease transaction reported. Maintenance and growth cash capex combined budgets, not verified contractual commitments. Depreciation2.6 crore grows8%, intentionally not the unreliable asset-by-asset allocation. Tax26%, 1% entry/exit friction, zero dividends. Cash gap means model funding need, not observed default. Dated market risks may exceed friction.

reverse_15pct_hurdle.caveat: Mechanical required revenue with the same capex budget and margins, not proof existing capacity can support it. Check liquidity of financing and additional capacity costs before adopting.
